title: Foundations: Indie Folk - The Complete Guide
summary: What Indie Folk is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Indie Folk songs: Folk songs are the people's music: songs passed mouth to ear across generations, built for singing together with simple instruments. The verse-chorus folk ballad form carries stories — love, work, loss, travel — on plain, sturdy melodies.

History: Folk ballads like Barbara Allen trace to 17th-century Britain and traveled to Appalachia with settlers, where singers reshaped them. The 1940s-60s folk revival (Woody Guthrie, Pete Seeger, Joan Baez, Bob Dylan) carried folk songs from porches to concert halls and protest marches.

How the songs work: Indie Folk favors the keys of G, C, D, A, Em. Common forms include Verse-chorus with a repeating refrain; Strophic: same melody, new words each verse; Call-and-response verse. Players should master carter scratch: bass note then strummed chord on each beat first, then travis picking: alternating thumb bass with melody on top strings. Capo 2 is the folk guitarist's best friend: play open G, C, D shapes in the bright key of A.

title: Scarborough Fair - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Scarborough Fair, a public-domain Indie Folk standard.
body:
Scarborough Fair (Traditional English ballad. Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Are you going to Scarborough Fair?
Parsley, sage, rosemary and thyme;
Remember me to one who lives there,
She once was a true love of mine.

Tell her to make me a cambric shirt,
Parsley, sage, rosemary and thyme;
Without no seams nor needlework,
Then she'll be a true love of mine.

Tell her to find me an acre of land,
Parsley, sage, rosemary and thyme;
Between the salt water and the sea strand,
Then she'll be a true love of mine.

Tell her to reap it with a sickle of leather,
Parsley, sage, rosemary and thyme;
And gather it all in a bunch of heather,
Then she'll be a true love of mine.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Indie Folk accompaniment in G using the 'Folk I–V–vi–IV' pattern:
G | D | Em | C

Technique: carter scratch: bass note then strummed chord on each beat. Capo 2 is the folk guitarist's best friend: play open G, C, D shapes in the bright key of A.
facts: Form: Verse-chorus with a repeating refrain

title: Greensleeves - Complete Public-Domain Song

body:

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Alas, my love, you do me wrong,
To cast me off discourteously.
For I have loved you well and long,
Delighting in your company.

Chorus:
Greensleeves was all my joy,
Greensleeves was my delight,
Greensleeves was my heart of gold,
And who but my lady Greensleeves.

I have been ready at your hand,
To grant whatever you would crave;
I have both wagered life and land,
Your love and good-will for to have.

title: Barbara Allen - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Barbara Allen, a public-domain Indie Folk standard.
body:
Barbara Allen (Traditional ballad (Child Ballad 84), 17th century. Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
In Scarlet town, where I was born,
There was a fair maid dwellin',
Made every youth cry Well-a-way!
Her name was Barbara Allen.

'Twas in the merry month of May,
When green buds they were swellin',
Sweet William on his death-bed lay,
For love of Barbara Allen.

He sent his servant unto her,
To the town where she was dwellin',
Saying, Master dear has sent me here,
If your name be Barbara Allen.

Slowly, slowly she got up,
And slowly she went nigh him,
And all she said when she got there,
Young man, I think you're dyin'.

He turned his face unto the wall,
And death was drawing nigh him:
Adieu, adieu, my dear friends all,
Be kind to Barbara Allen.

She looked to the east, she looked to the west,
She saw his corpse a-comin';
Lay down, lay down your corpse, she cried,
That I may gaze upon him.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Indie Folk accompaniment in D using the 'Folk lament vi–IV–I–V' pattern:
Dm | A# | F | C

Technique: capo to match the singer's range without relearning shapes. Capo 2 is the folk guitarist's best friend: play open G, C, D shapes in the bright key of A.
